title: An acyclic resolution representing the specified finite affine section complex
statement: Let f:X\to T be a separated quasi-compact morphism of schemes with affine T [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let F be a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let V:Fin(r)\to X.Opens be a finite affine open cover. Write G=f_* for ordinary module direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] and C=finiteAffineCechModel(f,F,V) [def-pc-finite-affine-cech-model]. There exist a complex D in nonnegative degrees of X-modules and an augmentation epsilon:F[0]\to D which is a quasi-isomorphism, whose every term is G-right-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic], and a chain isomorphism G(D extended by zero to integer degrees)\cong C. No derived localizations are supplied and no total derived isomorphism is part of this assertion.

source.place: Tags 01XB, 01XD, 01FK, 01FM and 01I6; increasing-tuple sheaf resolution and termwise affine tilde-Gamma identification

proof.text: Construct degree p as the finite product of open direct images of F on increasing (p+1)-tuple intersections, with signed restriction differential and restriction augmentation. The two orders of deleting entries cancel. The sheaf-product construction of the usual Cech resolution applies to these increasing tuples. On each cover member insert its index, sort with sign and annihilate repetitions; the face calculation contracts the augmentation. Equivalently apply the ordered comparison, compatibly with augmentation, to the usual sheaf Cech resolution. Thus epsilon is a quasi-isomorphism. Witnesses are consumed only in proofs.

Separatedness over the affine target makes every nonempty tuple intersection affine. Transport affine-open pushforward acyclicity along the canonical affine target isomorphism T to Spec Gamma(T,O). Each factor is f_*-acyclic, and the finite product is acyclic by closure of rightAcyclic under finite products. This also includes empty intersections and degrees with no increasing tuples.

On the canonical affine chart, the tilde-Gamma counit identifies each pushforward factor with its associated section module. Its restriction naturality identifies the signed differential. Finite products and extension by zero give a chain isomorphism of the ordinary pushed complex with finiteAffineCechModel, with exactly its GammaSpecIso scalar restriction and pullback to T. For r=0 the covering equality forces X empty, and the zero complex with unique augmentation supplies the claim.

CechSheafResolution gives an unnormalized resolution without the increasing-tuple ordinary chain comparison. CechResolution has a private derived comparison, but its AffineOpenPushforwardAcyclic import reaches the item through AffineMorphism and FiniteFreeComplex. AffineAlternatingCechResolutionCore requires universal derived-category instances and base-change data and also has a transitive import cycle. No usable exact underived resolution for this model.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteAffineCechModel_acyclic_resolution
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) [IsAffine T] [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    {r : ℕ} (V : Fin r → X.Opens) (hV : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i))
    (hcover : iSup V = ⊤) :
    ∃ (D : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ)
      (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ X.Modules).obj F ⟶ D),
      QuasiIso ε ∧
      (∀ p, (RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightAcyclic (D.X p)) ∧
      Nonempty (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (D.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ≅
          finiteAffineCechModel f F V)
